item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President states an executive policy and directs continuing protective efforts and creation of an internal coordinating board; implementation occurs through later executive-branch activity, with no present change to legal rights.","evidence":"The protection program authorized by this order shall consist of continuous efforts to secure information systems for critical infrastructure"},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The President establishes an internal executive board and assigns OMB advisory and oversight responsibilities; these are immediate organizational and management measures, not substantive legal consequences.","evidence":"I hereby establish the \"President's Critical Infrastructure Protection Board\""},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The Board, Secretary of Defense, and DCI are assigned support, oversight, policy-development, and implementation responsibilities concerning agency systems; these are internal management functions.","evidence":"shall have responsibility to oversee, develop, and ensure implementation of policies, principles, standards, and guidelines"},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"Executive officials must develop security policies, advise leadership, monitor programs, and maintain agency-system security; any operational consequences arise through later discretionary administration.","evidence":"the Secretary of Defense and the DCI shall develop policies, principles, standards, and guidelines"},{"segment_id":"5","code":1,"rationale":"Agency heads must develop and fund internal security programs within available appropriations; this directs executive program management rather than a specified legal outcome for regulated parties.","evidence":"shall ensure the development and, within available appropriations, funding of programs"},{"segment_id":"6","code":1,"rationale":"The Board and other executive officials receive extensive coordination, advisory, outreach, and organizational duties; these govern internal administration and voluntary cooperation rather than dictate legal consequences.","evidence":"the Board shall recommend policies and coordinate programs"},{"segment_id":"7","code":1,"rationale":"Departments and the Chair must share information and manage Board meetings, while the Chair may propose policies; these are internal reporting and management functions.","evidence":"The Chair, in consultation with the Board, shall call and preside at meetings of the Board and set the agenda for the Board."},{"segment_id":"8","code":1,"rationale":"The Chair is assigned an internal dual-reporting relationship, effective as an organizational measure without changing substantive legal rights.","evidence":"the Chair shall report to both the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs and to the Assistant to the President for Homeland Security"},{"segment_id":"9","code":1,"rationale":"The segment assigns coordination, staffing, personnel-detail, supervisory, and committee-formation authorities within the executive branch; these are internal organizational measures.","evidence":"The Board may establish standing and ad hoc committees as appropriate."},{"segment_id":"10","code":1,"rationale":"Committee chairs must report their activities to the Board; this is an internal reporting requirement with no external legal consequence.","evidence":"Chairs of standing and ad hoc committees shall report fully and regularly on the activities of the committees to the Board"},{"segment_id":"11","code":1,"rationale":"The Board must coordinate its committees, and the President establishes and assigns leadership to an internal standing committee; both are organizational measures.","evidence":"There are established the following standing committees"},{"segment_id":"12","code":1,"rationale":"The segment constitutes, renames, chairs, and assigns coordinating duties to Board committees; these changes reorganize executive administration without altering substantive rights.","evidence":"shall serve as a Board standing committee, and be redesignated the Committee on National Security Systems"},{"segment_id":"13","code":1,"rationale":"The standing committee is directed to coordinate its work with another executive office; this is internal coordination.","evidence":"The standing committee shall coordinate its work with the Office of Homeland Security"},{"segment_id":"14","code":1,"rationale":"The segment assigns committee coordination and assessment functions and authorizes formation of additional committees and subcommittees; these are internal organizational duties.","evidence":"The chair of each standing committee may form necessary subcommittees"},{"segment_id":"15","code":1,"rationale":"The Board must develop internal procedures for carrying out transferred responsibilities; the later procedures concern executive organization and do not dictate a substantive legal result.","evidence":"The Board shall develop procedures"},{"segment_id":"16","code":1,"rationale":"The Board must review an existing body's functions, recommend its future role, and propose plans; these are study, recommendation, and planning functions.","evidence":"shall review the functions of the Joint Telecommunications Resources Board"},{"segment_id":"17","code":1,"rationale":"The Board must review program needs and recommend budget treatment to OMB; it does not itself allocate funds or compel OMB to adopt a specified result.","evidence":"shall make recommendations to OMB"},{"segment_id":"18","code":1,"rationale":"Executive offices are directed or authorized to provide personnel, funding, and administrative support from available appropriations for an internal Board; this is administrative resourcing and housekeeping.","evidence":"shall provide the Board with such personnel, fund ing, and administrative support"},{"segment_id":"19","code":1,"rationale":"NSA must secure the Board's systems, while the Board may request research funding in agency budget submissions; these are internal operations and budget-planning functions.","evidence":"The National Security Agency shall ensure that the Board's information and communications systems are appropriately secured."},{"segment_id":"20","code":1,"rationale":"The Chair is directed to coordinate with presidential advisory panels, whose leaders may participate in Board meetings; this is internal advisory coordination.","evidence":"The Chair shall work closely with panels of senior experts from outside of the government that advise the President"},{"segment_id":"21","code":1,"rationale":"The President immediately creates a presidential advisory council, an internal organizational act expressly treated as Code 1 under the codebook.","evidence":"There is hereby established the National Infrastructure Advisory Council"},{"segment_id":"22","code":1,"rationale":"The segment defines the advisory council's function, size, composition, and membership qualifications; these are organizational and staffing provisions.","evidence":"The NIAC shall be composed of not more than 30 members appointed by the President."},{"segment_id":"23","code":1,"rationale":"The President assigns NIAC leadership and executive-director roles and directs advisory, monitoring, reporting, and recommendation functions; these are internal governance measures.","evidence":"The Chair of the Board established by this order will serve as the Executive Director of the NIAC."},{"segment_id":"24","code":1,"rationale":"NIAC must report and advise, while the Board coordinates and NIAC may conduct inquiries or form subcommittees; these are advisory and organizational functions.","evidence":"The NIAC may hold hearings, conduct inquiries, and establish subcommittees, as appropriate."},{"segment_id":"25","code":3,"rationale":"The segment itself fixes council members' compensation status immediately, while permitting legally authorized travel reimbursement; the no-compensation rule is a present substantive compensation consequence.","evidence":"Members shall serve without compensation for their work on the Council."},{"segment_id":"26","code":1,"rationale":"Commerce must furnish administrative support, receives delegated presidential advisory-committee functions, and the Council is given an internal sunset; these are administration, delegation, and organizational housekeeping.","evidence":"the functions of the President under that Act, except that of reporting to the Congress, shall be performed by the Department of Commerce"},{"segment_id":"27","code":1,"rationale":"The President revokes a prior order and directs NCS support while preserving existing assignments; under the codebook, revocation reorganizing administration and internal responsibility assignments are Code 1.","evidence":"Executive Order 13130 of July 14, 1999, is hereby revoked."},{"segment_id":"28","code":1,"rationale":"The Board must coordinate its activities with another executive office to address foreign intelligence threats; this is internal coordination.","evidence":"The Board shall coordinate its activities with those of the Office of the Counter-intelligence Executive"},{"segment_id":"29","code":1,"rationale":"The President delegates an existing presidential classification function to the Chair and preserves superior legal requirements; the codebook expressly treats delegation of presidential functions as internal management.","evidence":"I hereby delegate to the Chair the authority to classify information originally as Top Secret"}]}
